_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: Every one of the 54 files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-03 (run 30765982979, `weigh-tests.yml`) -- one file per job, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. Re-run that workflow and paste its block; do not hand-edit one number. The 2026-07-31 table covered 42 files and left 12 riding `_default_weight` 16 -- develop-context-pack.bats measured 49s against that 16, the same understatement `_evidence` records for shard 7.
_evidence: These weights are not asserted, they are checked. #73 shipped weights that predicted shard 7/12 at 111s; it ran 204s and then 198s, and it alone set the wall clock at 4m08. The re-measurement puts that shard's four files at 198s -- arc-scan 21->58, toolcheck 16->35, baseline 10->35, prune-report 64->70 -- which is the observed number, not a number near it. The 42 weights also now sum to 1593s against a real grouped windows total of 1585s measured independently, so the own-bats-call method predicts the invocation CI actually performs.
_floor: design-steel-thread.bats at 141s is the floor no shard count can beat -- from 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split across two runners. Going below ~2m50 means splitting it, or making one job run several bats processes at once.
_known_gap: These are WINDOWS seconds and the macOS leg is sharded with them, which is wrong in kind: the last 2-shard macOS split came out 77s and 161s against a prediction of 797/796, because the process-spawn cost that dominates windows does not dominate macOS. macOS is given a third shard to make the error small rather than a weights table of its own, since at 238s total it is not the binding leg. If it ever becomes one, weigh it on macos-latest instead of tuning the shard count.
